exam: Kerala PSC Divisional Accountant / Divisional Accounts Officer - Preliminary Examination
paper: Question Paper Code 50/2025, Booklet A (English medium), held 10-May-2025

questions.q: The last Lodi dynasty ruler of Delhi Sultanate.
questions.e: Ibrahim Lodi, defeated by Babur at Panipat in 1526, was the last Lodi Sultan of Delhi.

questions.q: Stamp Act and Townshend Act were related to which of the following?
questions.e: The British Stamp Act (1765) and Townshend Acts (1767) angered the colonists and led to the American War of Independence.

questions.q: Which of the following climate type is common to southern California, central Chile and southern tip of Africa?
questions.e: Dry summers and wet winters on the western sides of continents near 30-40° latitude mark the Mediterranean climate.

questions.q:
Below are the horizons of a mature soil profile. Arrange them in the proper sequence from surface to bed rock.
(i) A-Horizon, (ii) O-Horizon, (iii) B-Horizon, (iv) E-Horizon, (v) C-Horizon, (vi) R-Horizon
questions.e: From the surface down, a soil profile runs O, A, E, B, C and then R (bedrock).

questions.q: Among the following, which is the correct answer in national income estimation?
o: NNP at Market Price – Net Indirect Taxes = NNP at Factor Cost
NNP at Market Price + Depreciation = NNP at Factor Cost
GNP at Market Price – Net Indirect Taxes = NNP at Factor Cost
GNP at Market Price – Depreciation = NNP at Factor Cost
questions.e: Subtracting net indirect taxes from NNP at market price gives NNP at factor cost (national income).

questions.q: Among the following, which was the central objective of the 12th Five Year Plan?
o: High rate of growth, social justice and self-reliance
Growth, modernization, self-reliance and social justice
Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth
questions.e: The 12th Plan (2012-17) aimed at "Faster, more inclusive and sustainable growth".

questions.q: Who served as the Chief Guest at the Republic Day celebrations in India in 2025?
questions.e: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto was the chief guest at Republic Day 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India.
1. Section 213(1) of the Government of India Act, 1935 allowed the Federal Court to give advisory opinions to the Governor-General.
2. The Supreme Court has advisory jurisdiction on matters referred by the President under Article 143 of the Constitution.
3. The ruling of the Supreme Court is advisory and the President has the option to follow or not follow it.
4. The Supreme Court may choose to offer or refuse its opinion to the President on disputes arising from pre-Constitution treaties, agreements or covenants. Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.e: Art. 143 advisory opinions (descended from s.213 of the 1935 Act) are not binding; for pre-Constitution treaty disputes under 143(2) the Court must give its opinion, so statement 4 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements related to the Declaration of National Emergency in India.
1. The fundamental rights provided in Article 19 are automatically suspended.
2. Article 358 addresses the suspension of Article 19, while Article 359 pertains to the suspension of other fundamental rights.
3. Articles 20 and 21 (Right to life and personal liberty) cannot be suspended.
4. Other rights may be suspended by the President through a separate order issued to that effect. Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
o: All of the above are correct
questions.e: Art. 358 suspends Art. 19 automatically (for war or external aggression), Art. 359 lets the President suspend other rights, and Arts. 20-21 cannot be suspended, so all four are accepted.

questions.q: Who is known as the Father of All-India Services?
questions.e: Sardar Patel championed the creation of the IAS and IPS and is called the father of the All-India Services.

questions.q: The following are the titles of four famous novels written by M.T. Vasudevan Nair with the names of the central character noted against each. Identify the wrongly paired one among these.
questions.e: In M.T.'s Naalukettu the central character is Appunni, not Kunhunni.

questions.q: Gukesh Dommaraju became the FIDE World Chess Champion in 2024 by defeating which of the following players?
questions.e: D. Gukesh beat China's Ding Liren in Singapore in December 2024 to become world champion.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about operating system functions is NOT correct?
o: Process management in an operating system includes scheduling, execution and termination of processes.
Memory management ensures optimal allocation and deallocation of RAM to running processes.
The primary function of an operating system is to translate high-level programming code into machine code.
An operating system provides an interface between the user and the hardware.
questions.e: Translating high-level code into machine code is the job of a compiler or interpreter, not the OS.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an example of a search engine?
questions.e: Mozilla Firefox is a web browser; Google, Bing and Yahoo are search engines.

questions.q: Which of the following satellite was launched by ISRO to support television broadcasting and weather forecasting services?
questions.e: GSAT-24 is a communication satellite serving DTH television (for NSIL/Tata Play), the option the key marks.

questions.q: Choose the correct plural form of the word "goose":
questions.e: "Goose" has the irregular plural "geese".

questions.q: Which of the following is an auxiliary verb?
questions.e: "Will" is a modal auxiliary verb that helps form the future tense.

questions.q: Identify the past perfect tense in the sentence:
o: He had already left when I arrived.
questions.e: "Had left" (had + past participle) is the past perfect.

questions.q: Which sentence correctly uses a possessive pronoun?
questions.e: "Mine" and "hers" are both possessive pronouns; option B wrongly uses "it" instead of "its".

questions.q: Find the correctly spelled word:
questions.e: The correct spellings are receive, definitely, accommodate and occasion.

questions.q: Identify the countable noun from the list:
questions.e: "Chair" can be counted (one chair, two chairs); the others are uncountable.

questions.q: Choose the correct form of reported speech: He said, "I am reading a book".
o: He said he is reading a book.
He said that he was reading a book.
He said he read a book.
He says he was reading a book.
questions.e: In reported speech, "am reading" shifts back to "was reading".

questions.q: Select the correct sentence in active voice:
o: The letter was written by John.
The cake was eaten by the children.
The door was opened by the guard.
questions.e: "The teacher explains the lesson" has the doer as subject, so it is active voice.

questions.q: Choose the correct phrasal verb to complete the sentence: The firemen were able to _______ the fire before it spread.
questions.e: To "put out" a fire means to extinguish it.

questions.q: Which sentence contains an adjective?
o: The tall building is visible from here.
questions.e: "Tall" describes the noun "building", so it is an adjective.

questions.q: Identify the irregular verb from the options:
questions.e: "Buy" has the irregular past form "bought".

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence using a preposition:
o: He is waiting since two hours.
I am interested in learning French.
They are married with five years.
questions.e: "Interested in" is the correct collocation; the others should be "for two hours", "angry with" and "married for".

questions.q: Identify the sentence with a correctly used idiom:
o: She hit the roof when she heard the news.
The exam was a piece of cake, but I failed.
I am feeling under the sky today.
questions.e: "Hit the roof" means to become very angry, and it is used correctly here.

questions.q: Choose the correctly jumbled sentence:
o: Always park the in evening I.
In the park, I always walk in the evening.
Evening in I the park walk always.
Walk in evening always the I park.
questions.e: Only option B is a grammatical, meaningful sentence.

questions.q:
Which of the following statement is/are true about a journal?
(i) Journal is the book of prime entry.
(ii) Journal is prepared to classify business transactions.
(iii) Business transactions are recorded in the journal only after being recorded in the ledger.
questions.e: The journal is the book of original entry; classifying is the ledger's job, and journal entries come before ledger posting.

questions.q:
"Distribution of goods as samples" is recorded in the books of accounts by
(i) Debiting 'Purchases Account' and Crediting 'Cash Account'.
(ii) Debiting 'Advertising Account' and Crediting 'Purchases Account'.
(iii) Debiting 'Drawings Account' and Crediting 'Purchases Account'.
questions.e: Free samples are a promotion expense: debit Advertisement A/c and credit Purchases A/c.

questions.q:
Which among the following is/are not an objective of 'Trial Balance'?
(i) To show the financial position of the business.
(ii) To check the correctness of book-keeping work.
(iii) To ascertain the profit or loss of the business.
questions.e: A trial balance only checks the arithmetical accuracy of the ledger; it shows neither the financial position nor profit or loss.

questions.q: Which among the following is the correct statement as regards a Trading Account and a Profit and Loss Account?
o: Trading account shows net profit, and profit & loss account shows gross profit.
Trading account deals with direct expenses & revenue, and the profit & loss account deals with indirect expenses.
Trading account shows liabilities, and profit & loss account shows assets.
questions.e: The Trading A/c records direct expenses and sales to find gross profit, and the P&L A/c records indirect expenses.

questions.q: The stock of uninsured goods destroyed by fire is
o: Debited to Trading Account and credited to Profit and Loss Account
Debited to Profit and Loss Account and taken to the Balance Sheet as a liability
Debited to Trading Account and taken to the Balance Sheet as a liability
Credited to Trading Account and debited to Profit and Loss Account
questions.e: Uninsured stock lost by fire is credited to the Trading A/c (removing it from goods) and debited to P&L as a loss.

questions.q: The prepaid insurance at the beginning of an accounting year will be adjusted in the books by
o: Crediting Insurance Account and debiting Prepaid Insurance Account.
Debiting Insurance Account and crediting Prepaid Insurance Account.
Debiting Profit and Loss Account and crediting Insurance Account.
questions.e: Opening prepaid insurance becomes this year's expense: debit Insurance A/c, credit Prepaid Insurance A/c.

questions.q: Which among the following is not a cause of depreciation?
questions.e: Depreciation comes from use, passage of time and obsolescence; market trends are not a cause.

questions.q: Choose the correct statement from the following:
o: Provisions are charge against profit generally created for meeting a specific liability in future.
Provisions are debited to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account.
The amount transferred to the General Reserve Account can be deducted from profit for arriving at the taxable profit.
General Reserve is taken to the asset side of the Balance Sheet.
questions.e: A provision is a charge against profit for a known future liability.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about secret reserves is correct?
o: Secret reserves are considered unethical as they conceal the true financial position of a company.
Accounting standards recommend secret reserves to improve transparency.
Secret reserves are disclosed in financial statements under "Other Reserves".
Secret reserves are easily identifiable and transparent in financial audits.
questions.e: Secret reserves hide the true financial position, so they are considered unethical and are restricted.

questions.q: Choose the most appropriate statement from the following: Endorsement is
o: The process of signing a negotiable instrument.
The process of transfer of a negotiable instrument.
The process of honouring a negotiable instrument on the due date.
The process of signing on the back of a negotiable instrument for negotiation.
questions.e: Endorsement is signing on the back of a negotiable instrument to negotiate (transfer) it.

questions.q: Which among the following is not a characteristic feature of a Bill of Exchange?
o: It is an instrument in writing.
It is signed by the maker.
It directs a certain person to pay a certain sum of money.
questions.e: A bill contains an unconditional order to pay; an unconditional promise is a feature of a promissory note.

questions.q: An additional piece of paper attached to a negotiable instrument to provide space for endorsements when the original document has insufficient space is
questions.e: An allonge is a slip attached to an instrument when there is no room left for endorsements.

questions.q: The expenses associated with procuring and utilizing fuel to power a vessel's engines during maritime operations is
questions.e: Bunker cost is the cost of fuel (bunkers) for the ship's engines.

questions.q:
Choose the correct statement/s connected to Voyage Accounts from the following:
(i) Primage is the additional freight collected in a voyage, which is credited to the Voyage Account.
(ii) Address Commission is the amount payable to the agents for procuring cargo, which is credited to the Voyage Account.
(iii) Stevedoring Charges are related to loading and unloading cargo and are debited to the Voyage Account.
(iv) Passage Money is collected from the passengers who travel, which is debited to the Voyage Accounts.
questions.e: Primage is extra freight (credited) and stevedoring is a loading/unloading expense (debited); address commission is debited and passage money credited.

questions.q: If a voyage is incomplete at the end of the accounting year, how should the freight related to the incomplete voyage be treated?
o: Credited to Voyage Account and debited to Voyage-in-progress Account.
Debited to Voyage Account and credited to Voyage-in-progress Account.
Ignored while preparing the Voyage Account.
questions.e: The unearned share of freight on an incomplete voyage is debited to the Voyage A/c and carried forward to Voyage-in-progress.

questions.q: In a self-balancing ledger system, the total of the Purchases Ledger Adjustment Account should match with the total of which ledger?
questions.e: The Purchases Ledger Adjustment A/c in the general ledger agrees with the total of the purchases (creditors) ledger.

questions.q: Why are self-balancing ledgers useful in large organizations?
o: They make it easier to detect errors and fraud
They remove the need for accounting software
questions.e: Because each ledger balances on its own, errors and frauds can be located easily.

questions.q:
Statement 1 : Errors in a self-balancing ledger can be identified quickly.
Statement 2 :  A separate trial balance is prepared for each ledger, making error detection easier.
o: Statement 1 is Correct, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is Correct
questions.e: A separate trial balance for each ledger allows errors to be traced quickly, so both statements are correct.

questions.q:
Statement 1 : Capital expenditure is treated as a long-term investment and is charged as an expense in the Profit & Loss Account.
Statement 2 : Revenue expenditure is treated as long term investment and is charged as expense in the Profit & Loss Account.
o: Statement 1 is Correct, Statement 2 is False
Statement 1 is False, Statement 2 is Correct
questions.e: Capital expenditure is capitalised, not charged to P&L, and revenue expenditure is not a long-term investment, so both statements are false.

questions.q: Which statement is true about the Receipts & Payments Account and Income & Expenditure Account?
o: Both are prepared on an accrual basis
Receipts & Payments Account records cash transactions, while Income & Expenditure Account records accrual transactions
Both are used to determine surplus or deficit
questions.e: The Receipts & Payments A/c is a cash summary, while the Income & Expenditure A/c follows the accrual basis.

questions.q: The formula for calculating cost of production is
questions.e: Cost of production = factory (works) cost + office and administration overheads.

questions.q: If the selling price per unit is ₹200 and the total cost per unit is ₹160, then what is the profit percentage on cost?
questions.e: Profit = 40 on a cost of 160, i.e. 25%.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
o: Prime cost includes all direct and indirect costs
Factory cost is also known as cost of goods manufactured
Selling overheads are added to cost of production to get factory cost
Financial charges are included in a cost sheet
questions.e: Factory (works) cost is also called the cost of goods manufactured.

questions.q: Total factory overheads are ₹1,20,000. If direct wages are ₹80,000 and factory overheads are absorbed based on a percentage of direct wages, then what is the overhead absorption rate?
A contract has a total cost of ₹7,50,000 and the total contract price is ₹10,00,000. The contractor receives 75% of work certified which is ₹7,50,000. What is the retention money?
Which financial statement in the Double Account System provides details of the fixed assets and how they were financed?
questions.e: The Receipts and Expenditure on Capital Account shows fixed assets and how they were financed.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of the Double Account System?
o: It does not provide separate treatment for capital and revenue items
Not suitable for all types of businesses
questions.e: The system does separate capital and revenue items, so that is not one of its limitations.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a limitation of the Double Account System?
o: It does not provide a true financial position
It is difficult to apply in non-utility sectors
It allows easy comparison of financial performance
questions.e: Easy comparison of performance is a benefit, not a limitation.

questions.q: What is the least number which when divided by 8, 9, 12, 15 leaves remainder as 1 in each case?
Find the sum of the factors of 3240.
questions.e: 3240 = 2³·3⁴·5, so the sum of factors = 15 × 121 × 6 = 10890.

questions.q: The graph of a polynomial intersects the Y-axis at one point and the X-axis at two points. The number of zeros of this polynomial are
questions.e: The number of zeros equals the number of points where the graph cuts the x-axis, here 2.

questions.q: If the sum of zeros of the quadratic polynomial 3x² – kx + 6 is 3, then the value of k is
questions.e: The sum of zeros = k/3 = 3, so k = 9.

questions.q: When the equation is multiplied or divided by same non-zero number on both sides, the solution of the equation
questions.e: Multiplying or dividing both sides by the same non-zero number gives an equivalent equation with the same solution.

questions.q: The cost of 2 tables and 4 chairs is Rs. 16,000 while the cost of one table is equal to the cost of 6 chairs. Find the cost of 9 chairs.
questions.e: A table costs 6 chairs, so 2T + 4C = 16C = 16000 and C = 1000; 9 chairs cost 9000.

questions.q: 2 × 3 × 7 is the prime factorization of a particular number. Which among the following is the square of that number?
questions.e: The number is 42, and 42² = 1764.

questions.q: Sn denotes the sum of first n terms of an AP. If S40 = 1030 and S12 = 57, then S30 – S10 is equal to
The sum of first three terms of an AP is 30 and sum of the last three terms is 36. If the first term is 9, then the number of terms is
questions.e: The first three terms sum to 30, so a₂ = 10 and d = 1; the last three sum to 36, so the second-last term is 12 and the series is 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 (5 terms).

questions.q: A trader mixes 26 Kg of rice at Rs. 20 per Kg with 30 Kg of rice of other variety at Rs. 36 per Kg and sells the mixture at Rs. 30 per Kg. His profit percentage is

The percentage profit earned by selling an article for Rs.1920 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same article for Rs.1280. At what price should the article be sold to make 25% profit?
questions.e: Equal profit and loss % means CP = (1920 + 1280)/2 = 1600; 125% of 1600 = 2000.

questions.q: u : v = 4 : 7 and v : w = 9 : 7. If u = 72, then what is the value of w?
questions.e: u:v:w = 36:63:49; u = 72 means a multiplier of 2, so w = 98.

questions.q: The ratio of Rahul's and Remya's present age is 9:10. After 4 years, the ratio of their ages becomes 11:12. What is Rahul's present age?
questions.e: (9x + 4)/(10x + 4) = 11/12 gives x = 2, so Rahul is 18.

questions.q: Two numbers are less than a third number by 30% and 37% respectively. How much percent is the second number less than the first?
questions.e: If the third number is 100, the first two are 70 and 63; 7/70 = 10%.

questions.q: A number is first decreased by 20% and then increased by 15%. The number so obtained is 64 less than the original number. The original number is
questions.e: 0.8 × 1.15 = 0.92, so a 8% fall equals 64 and the number is 800.

questions.q: The difference of compound interest and simple interest on a principal amount for two years at 4% per annum is Rs.20. The principal is

A man borrowed some money and agreed to pay off by paying Rs.3150 at the end of first year and Rs.4410 at the end of second year. If the rate of compound interest is 5% per annum, then the amount borrowed is
If A = {(x, y) : x² + y² < 1, x, y ∈ ℝ} and B = {(x, y) : x² + y² < 4, x, y ∈ ℝ}, then
questions.e: A (the disc of radius 1) lies inside B (radius 2), so A − B is empty.

questions.q: The arithmetic mean of 12 observations is 20. If two observations 15 and 25 are removed, then the arithmetic mean of the remaining observations is
questions.e: Total 240 − 40 = 200 over 10 observations, giving a mean of 20.

questions.q: If the centroid of a triangle with vertices (1, x), (2, y) and (x + y, 2) lies on x-axis, then
questions.e: The centroid's y-coordinate (x + y + 2)/3 = 0, so x + y = −2.

questions.q: The minimum and maximum values of 6 sin x cos x + 4 cos 2x are respectively,
questions.e: 6 sin x cos x + 4 cos 2x = 3 sin 2x + 4 cos 2x, which ranges from −5 to 5.

questions.q: ABC and BDE are two equilateral triangles such that D is mid-point of BC. Ratio of the areas of triangles ABC to BDE is
questions.e: BDE has half the side of ABC, so the area ratio is 2² : 1 = 4 : 1.

questions.q: The least number of square tiles required to pave the floor of a room, 15 meter 17 centimetre long and 9 meter 2 centimetre broad is
The volume of two spheres are in the ratio 64 : 27. If the sum of their radii is 7, then the difference of their surface area is
questions.e: The radii ratio is 4:3 with sum 7, so r = 4, 3; the difference in surface area = 4π(16 − 9) = 28π ≈ 88 sq.cm.

questions.q: A red light flashes 3 times per minute and a green light flashes 5 times in two minutes at regular intervals. If both lights start flashing at the same time, then how many times do they flash together within half an hour?
questions.e: Red flashes every 20 s and green every 24 s; they coincide every 120 s, i.e. 15 times in 30 minutes.

questions.q: A man makes a trip by automobile at an average speed of 60 km/hr. He returns over the same route at an average speed of 48 km/hr. His average speed for the entire trip is
questions.e: Average speed = 2 × 60 × 48 / (60 + 48) = 53⅓ km/hr.

questions.q: The difference between simple interest and compound interest on Rs.1200 for one year at 10% per annum reckoned half-yearly is
questions.e: CI = 1200(1.05² − 1) = 123 and SI = 120, a difference of 3.

questions.q: If selling price is doubled, the profit triples. Then the profit percent is
questions.e: 2S − C = 3(S − C) gives S = 2C, i.e. 100% profit.

questions.q: Two equal circles in the same plane cannot have the following number of common tangents
questions.e: Exactly one common tangent needs internal touching, which is impossible for equal distinct circles.

questions.q: The radius of the first circle is 1 cm, that of the second is 1/2 cm, that of the third is 1/4 cm and so on indefinitely. The sum of the areas of the circles is
The sides of a right triangle are a, a + d and a + 2d with a and d are positive. The ratio of a to d is
questions.e: a² + (a + d)² = (a + 2d)² gives a = 3d, so a : d = 3 : 1.

questions.q: The sides of a rectangle not a square are whole numbers. What must be their length such that the perimeter of the rectangle is numerically equal to the area?
questions.e: For 6 × 3: perimeter 18 = area 18.
